pages.text: Drop any armor into a Tetra workbench's input slot — it comes back $(bold)Reforged$(): modular, hone-able, and ready for upgrades.$(br2)This is Tetra's module-and-honing framework brought to the armor slot. Vanilla iron, an ISS Cultist Hood, Aether Phoenix, an Aquaculture diving helmet — all of it reforges.$(br2)Specialized armor keeps its identity. Vanilla armor gets the modular shape with a default-tier module pre-installed.

pages.title: How to reforge
pages.text: $(bold)Place the source armor in the workbench input slot.$() The replacement happens automatically.$(br2)$(bold)Specialized armor keeps its identity:$() the source's school spell power, set bonus, Apotheosis affixes, and enchantments all carry through — and the armor keeps its original look.$(br2)$(bold)Vanilla iron/gold/diamond/netherite$() get the modular shape with an iron-tier module pre-installed — upgrade it at the workbench.

pages.title: Module slots
pages.text: Each reforged piece has 2 slots:$(br2)$(thing)Helmet$() — crown (major) + visor (minor)$(br)$(thing)Chestplate$() — chest plate (major) + chest lining (minor)$(br)$(thing)Leggings$() — leg plate (major) + belt (minor)$(br)$(thing)Boots$() — boot sole (major) + boot lining (minor)$(br2)Major slots take metal materials and provide armor scaling with metal tier. Minor slots take fabric/leather/fibre (generic utility) OR themed materials (identity-flavored bonuses).

pages.title: Major slot bonuses (armor scaling)
pages.text: $(bold)Crown / chest plate / leg plate / boot sole$() — apply a metal, armor scales with the metal's tier.$(br2)$(thing)iron$() — modest baseline$(br)$(thing)gold$() — low armor, more enchantability$(br)$(thing)diamond$() — solid mid-tier$(br)$(thing)netherite$() — top vanilla tier$(br2)Modded metals (manasteel, knightmetal, ignitium, and friends) plug in automatically as their mods register them — higher-tier metal, higher armor.

pages.title: Minor slot bonuses — generic
pages.text: Apply $(thing)wool$(), $(thing)string$(), or $(thing)leather$() for the baseline utility:$(br2)$(thing)visor$() — +0.5 armor$(br)$(thing)chest lining$() — +5% mana regen$(br)$(thing)belt$() — +2% knockback resistance$(br)$(thing)boot lining$() — +0.2% movement speed$(br2)Cheap entry-level option — upgrade to themed materials later for identity bonuses.

pages.title: Minor slot bonuses — themed
pages.text: Apply axis-themed materials for identity-flavored bonuses. The 8 axes:$(br2)$(thing)Fire$() — blaze rod$(br)$(thing)Ice$() — blue ice$(br)$(thing)Shadow$() — ghast tear$(br)$(thing)Holy$() — glowstone dust$(br)$(thing)Lightning$() — redstone$(br)$(thing)Nature$() — sapling (mana regen instead of a school)$(br)$(thing)Ender$() — ender pearl$(br)$(thing)Blood$() — rotten flesh$(br2)Each theme grants $(item)+5% school spell power$() on the visor, $(item)+4%$() + mana regen on chest lining, $(item)+3%$() + KB resist on belt, $(item)+3%$() + speed on boot lining.

pages.title: Stack identity bonuses
pages.text: Themed minors stack with specialized skin attributes — that's the design.$(br2)$(thing)Cultist Hood$() (skin gives +5% blood spell power) + $(thing)Shadow visor$() (+5% blood) → $(item)+10% blood spell power$() on the helmet.$(br2)$(thing)Phoenix Robe$() + $(thing)Fire lining$() → $(item)+4% fire spell power$() + $(item)+4% mana regen$() added to the chestplate.$(br2)Mixing axes is allowed but usually wasteful — match the axis to what the skin already gives.

pages.title: Honing
pages.text: Each slot has a 5-level honing track scaling its signature stat:$(br2)$(thing)Helmet$() — armor toughness (+0.5 to +3.0)$(br)$(thing)Chestplate$() — armor (+0.5 to +3.0)$(br)$(thing)Leggings$() — knockback resistance (+0.02 to +0.10)$(br)$(thing)Boots$() — movement speed (+0.001 to +0.005)$(br2)Hone with the same hammer tiers as spellbooks: gold (L1), iron (L2), steel (L3), diamond (L4), netherite (L5).$(br2)At L3, apply the $(bold)settled$() schematic to lock the slot's identity and gain a small cross-stat bonus.

pages.title: Specialized skin coverage
pages.text: Dozens of specialized sets carry their signature attributes through reforging — ISS, Aether, Twilight Forest, Cataclysm, Aquaculture, Forbidden & Arcanus, Undergarden, Deeper & Darker, Botania, Blue Skies, and Deep Aether among them.$(br2)Each set's armor, toughness, Spell Power, and school-specific Spell Power survive the conversion, and the set keeps its original appearance.

pages.title: Set bonuses
pages.text: $(bold)Set bonuses persist through reforging.$() Wear 4 reforged pieces sharing one set identity and the original full-set bonus fires automatically:$(br2)$(thing)Phoenix$() — fire immunity$(br)$(thing)Neptune$() — water breathing + dolphin's grace$(br)$(thing)Aquaculture Neptunium$() — water breathing$(br)$(thing)Yeti$() — strength$(br)$(thing)Gravitite$() — jump boost II$(br)$(thing)Ignitium / Fiery$() — fire immunity$(br2)Mixed sets lose the set bonus; per-piece base attributes still apply.$(br2)$(bold)Next: drop a spare iron chestplate into a Tetra workbench and see it happen.$()
